fields.value: Supplemental materials for publications concerning three experiments with four songs

dsDescriptionValue.value: Stimuli and questionnaires underlying several articles. Plus EEG and GSR data.

publicationCitation.value: Schotanus, Y.P., Singing as a figure of speech, music as punctuation: A study into music as a means to support the processing of sung language [dissertation] (submitted)

Schotanus, Y. P. (2016). Well Tempered Tuning Cannot Account for Low Purity Ratings of Isolated Voice Parts, In: Zanto, T.P. (Ed.), Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Music Perception & Cognition (ICMPC14), July 2016, San Francisco, pp. 762-766. Adelaide: Causal Productions.

Schotanus, Y. P. (2016c). Music supports the processing of song lyrics and changes their contents: Effects of melody, silences, and accompaniment [Abstract], In: Zanto, T.P. (Ed.), Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Music Perception & Cognition (ICMPC14), July 2016, San Francisco, p. 361. Adelaide: Causal Productions. (Full text available on Researchegate and AcademiaEdu, and in Schotanus, 2017).

Schotanus, Y. P., Eekhof, L. S., & Willems, R. M. (2018). Behavioral and neurophysiological effects of singing and accompaniment on the perception and cognition of song. In Parncutt, R. & Sattmann, S. (Eds). Proceedings of ICMPC15/ESCOM10, pp. 389-394. Graz, Austria: Centre for Systematic Musicology, University of Graz.
Schotanus, Y. P. (submitted). Both singing and accompaniment support the processing of song lyrics and change the lyrics’ interpretation. Empirical Musicology Review.
Schotanus, Y. P. (submitted) The meaning of a song without the words. Music Perception.

fields.value: In this repository you will find the questionnaires (in Dutch), the stimuli (six versions of four songs, plus one or two additional versions per song) used in the papers mentioned above, and the 'leadsheets' representing those stimuli.

value: Schotanus, Y, 2020, "Supplementary materials PhD project Singing as a figure of speech and related publications", https://hdl.handle.net/10411/XRMMFW, DataverseNL, Handle
